content:
Let \(w\) be the date of the first Wednesday.  
- If \(w=1,\dots,6\), the first Thursday is \(w+1\). Common days satisfy  
  \[
  w+4m=w+1+3n \implies 4m-3n=1.
  \]
  The smallest solution is \(m=n=1\), so common days are
  \[
  w+4+12k.
  \]
  Since \(w+4\le 10\) and \(w+16\le 22\le 31\), there are at least two common days in January.

- If \(w=7\), the first Thursday is January 1. Then
  \[
  7+4m=1+3n \implies 3n-4m=6,
  \]
  giving common days \(7,19,31\), again three days.

Thus no possible first Wednesday gives exactly one common visit day in January.

\[
\boxed{\text{No such date exists}}
\]
